doc.title: Roger Kellaway interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Not listening to music and working with Paula Cole on Call Me Irresponsible
summary: He rarely listens to recordings; Paula Cole's session and his new management.

story.theme_name: Still working: current gigs, upcoming projects and plans
story.community_name: What's next: upcoming tours, records and plans

blocks.x: How often do you hear things these days that you’re playing on?
Well not very often because I don’t listen to anything that would tell me.
I have so little time that it turns out, to listen. When I’m driving, quite often it’s in silence and fortunately I’m blessed with a wife that also agrees with the concept.
I’ll bet there’s not silence in your head.

Well I can be driving along and looking at a mountain range and just enjoying that existence without a great deal of mental mess. I’m still trying to think of this tune that I recorded with Paula Cole on Sammy Cahn.
Can you hum it? I guess if you remembered the name you could hum it right away.

So it’s a duet with Paula Cole. She came in and sang beautifully, and I still really don’t know who she is musically. I know she’s a big star and she got five Grammys last year and all of that. But in our meeting she wanted me to dictate what I wanted her to sing, in solfege. So right away my opinion about here shot up about 25 points.
That she even knew the word, right?

Yeah. And I said, in my arrogance, okay, moveable do or fixed do? She said moveable do. I said great, okay. So I mean I hadn’t even thought about solfege in probably 30 years. So we’re doing all the chromatics and everything and I’m teaching her the lines to solfege. And wow, it was great. And she sung beautifully. So that’s the duet. That will probably be AM crossover. So there’s that and the new cello quartet project and I’m taking on a new agent for film and Gary George is my new manager and he’s someone that — I worked for a couple of his clients years ago. He feels strongly about the film area, and I like that idea.
